messages:
marta: Heads-up — I want to replace the old gpu-summary dashboard with a focused view: per-rack utilization, memory pressure, thermal distribution, PDU power trends, and an idle-GPU panel for provisioning/cost. Need panel ideas + alert thresholds before I draft the JSON.
liam: +1. Important to keep cardinality low (rack, region, model). For metrics we use dcgm_exporter and node exporter; some useful PromQL sketches: 
```
# memory % per GPU
avg by(gpu_id) (dcgm_gpu_fb_memory_used_bytes / dcgm_gpu_fb_memory_total_bytes) * 100
# max temp per GPU
max by(gpu_id) (dcgm_gpu_temp_celsius)
# power draw per rack
sum by(rack) (dcgm_gpu_power_usage_watts)
```
kevin: Also add aggregated percentiles so the heatmap isn't noisy. e.g., 95th for memory and power. And label fallback if rack missing -> zone. Watch cardinality on gpu_id in long-lived dashboards.
jordan: For alerts I'd propose: 
- GPUHighMemoryPressure: avg_over_time(dcgm_gpu_fb_memory_used_bytes / dcgm_gpu_fb_memory_total_bytes > 0.92)[5m] for 5m -> P1 (risk of OOMs)
- GPUOverTemp: avg_over_time(dcgm_gpu_temp_celsius > 85)[3m] -> P1, auto-shed non-critical workloads
- PowerCapApproach: ratio of power_draw / power_cap > 0.95 for 10m -> P2 (possible throttling)
Keep rules simple soops can triage quickly.
marta: Layout thinking: top-row fleet KPIs (utilization %, avg temp, % GPUs at power cap, free GPUs), second-row region heatmap (color by 95p mem), third-row racks: sparklines of temp/power and a table of top noisy GPUs. Drilldowns to logs (loki) + allocation traces. Thoughts?
tiago: Panel types: Stat with sparkline for KPI, Heatmap for temp distribution, Gauge for power headroom (but set with trend overlay), Table for noisy GPUs (sort by stddev temp or frequent context switches). Add a histogram bucket for allocation duration to spot short-lived churn.
liam: Add template variables: region, rack, model, allocation_pool. Also add a low-cardinality "health_tag" to group rented vs dedicated. And precompute a `gpu_idle_minutes_total` counter so we can derive idle minutes per GPU per day for cost analysis.
kevin: Provisioning angle: expose a panel with "idle GPU minutes" per zone and an estimated cost column (use on-demand price label). Autoscaler rule suggestion: spin new nodes when avg_free_gpus_in_region < 8 for 15m; scale down when avg_free_gpus_in_region > 30 for 60m (avoid thrash). We'll want these knobs in the dashboard for on-call to adjust temporarily.
marta: I'll include a small runbook link and a one-click link that opens the allocation page for the selected rack. Plan: export current panels as JSON, refactor rows, add variables, then open a PR. Will mark the PR as RFC for review.
sre-bot: deploy-bot: grafana/dashboard/gpu-rack-heatmap json pushed to staging (sha: d4f3a2) — staged at https://grafana.staging/redwood/d/gpu-rack-heatmap
jordan: Nice, will review the panel JSON tonight. quick notes: prefer 5m for most query windows, use 1m for tight thermal spikes, and document the alert rationale inline. :thumbsup:
marta: Thanks all — I'll push a draft by EOD and tag reviewers. If anyone has a small example of the noisy-gpu table query, paste it here and I'll copy it into the PR.
liam: Example noisy GPU query (table): 
```
topk(10, by (gpu_id) (stddev_over_time(dcgm_gpu_temp_celsius[1h])))
```
kevin: And add this derived metric for idle minutes: 
```
increase(gpu_idle_seconds_total[1d]) / 60
```
marta: perfect, thanks — closing thread and starting the PR now. :rocket:
